scope.summary: One-open-edition-request-per-PDB is scoped to the service state store: the production HTTP draft route derives DBID/CON scope server-side and persists coordination_scope service_state_store; the in-process CREATE EDITION reservation is one board per service shared by every stateful HTTP session dispatcher; independent services do not claim exclusivity and Oracle's one-child rule (ORA-38807) decides a real race.
out_of_scope: Cross-deployment shared coordination backend; the rest of W12 (T12.2).

limitations: The identity field named con_uid is populated from SYS_CONTEXT CON_ID (USERENV CON_UID raised ORA-02003); CON_ID is stable within one CDB but is not the unplug/plug-stable CON_UID the finding names.
The in-process two-independent-services unit test still models ORA-38807 with a mock; the Oracle behaviour is proven by the separate live race test.

At d3c68ae7 itself no committed test covers cross-session sharing; that test lands in b2470901 (local, not yet on origin/main at verification time). Production sharing is additionally shown by code reading: stateful HTTP clones DispatcherWiring per session, cloning the one Arc board. No live multi-session HTTP race was run.
